title: Mohammed and the Pond That Went Quiet

pages.text: Behind the school garden lay a small shallow pond ringed with stones. Frogs croaked, tiny fish flashed in the water, and insects buzzed over green reeds and lily pads. “This pond is an ecosystem,” said the teacher. “It is a community of living things and the non-living things around them—such as water, air, sunlight, and soil. They all depend on one another.”
sentences: Behind the school garden lay a small shallow pond ringed with stones.
Frogs croaked, tiny fish flashed in the water, and insects buzzed over green reeds and lily pads.
“This pond is an ecosystem,” said the teacher.
“It is a community of living things and the non-living things around them—such as water, air, sunlight, and soil.
They all depend on one another.”
pages.alt: Mohammed, Baah, and their teacher stand safely behind a stone border watching green frogs, tiny fish, reeds, and dragonflies in a lively school pond.

pages.text: One Saturday after compound cleanup, Mohammed and Baah walked past the pond. “Those water weeds look messy,” said Mohammed. Standing on the dry bank with long wooden rakes, they pulled out the water plants to make the pond look tidy, not knowing the plants gave shade, food, and hiding places.
sentences: One Saturday after compound cleanup, Mohammed and Baah walked past the pond.
“Those water weeds look messy,” said Mohammed.
Standing on the dry bank with long wooden rakes, they pulled out the water plants to make the pond look tidy, not knowing the plants gave shade, food, and hiding places.
pages.alt: Standing back on the dry grass bank, Mohammed and Baah use long wooden rakes to pull green reeds and floating plants from the pond edge.

pages.text: Two weeks later, the pond had fallen quiet. Without shade, the water turned warm and murky. Fewer frogs called, the dragonflies disappeared, and the little fish had nowhere to shelter. “Where is all the croaking?” asked Baah worriedly. “Something is wrong. Let us tell Madam.”

pages.alt: Mohammed and Baah stand anxiously behind the stone border looking at a bare, silent pond with murky green water and empty banks.

pages.text: Their teacher listened kindly at the pondside. “Every member of an ecosystem has an important job,” she explained. “Plants give food, oxygen, cool shade, and shelter, while frogs and fish eat insects. Removing one member upsets the natural balance, so others suffer.” Mohammed looked down. “We caused this by mistake.”

pages.alt: Beside the bare pond, the teacher explains gently to remorseful Mohammed and thoughtful Baah, holding out her two hands like a steady balance.

pages.text: “How can we help fix it?” asked Baah. “We can replant native water plants together,” said the teacher. Wearing rubber boots while the class stayed safely back on firm ground, she guided them in replanting reeds and water lilies. Everyone promised to ask a teacher before changing any habitat again.

pages.alt: Supervised by their teacher in rubber boots at the shallow margin, Mohammed, Baah, and classmates pass green water plants from firm dry ground.

pages.text: After several weeks, the pond came alive once more. Frogs croaked in the cool green shade, fish darted safely among the stems, and dragonflies hummed above the leaves. “Every part matters,” said Mohammed happily. “Even the plants that look wild!” Together the class painted a nature mural celebrating their school habitat.

pages.alt: Beside the thriving pond full of frogs, reeds, and dragonflies, Mohammed, Baah, and classmates smile next to a wordless wall mural of hands cradling a leaf and frog.

activities.question: Why did the school pond fall quiet after the water plants were removed?
options: Pond animals lost their cool shade, food, and hiding places
All the water froze into solid ice
The frogs went on holiday to town

activities.question: What makes up an ecosystem?
options: Living things and the non-living things around them

activities.prompt: Put the pond ecosystem story in order.
items: Mohammed and Baah raked out the pond plants.
The pond grew warm, bare, and quiet.
With their teacher, the class replanted native water plants.
Frogs, fish, and insects returned as balance was restored.

activities.definition: A healthy, steady state in nature where living and non-living parts support one another.
distractors: A long wooden rake for clearing leaves
A stone wall around a garden

glossary.definition: A community of living things interacting with non-living things such as water, air, sunlight, and soil.
To rely on or need something else in order to survive and thrive.
A healthy, steady state in which each part of an ecosystem supports the others.
